facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2006 but lived together only for a short period. The relationship became strained and the wife left her husband's company. The husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia) & (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which was dismissed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: The prayer for restitution of conjugal rights cannot be granted if the parties have been living separately for a long time.
legal_principles.held: Undisputably, after the Family Court had passed the ex-parte judgment against the appellant-wife in M.C.No.539/2007, the respondent-husband had remarried on 28.10.2009 and from the said wedlock a girl child is born. It is also not in dispute the parties are residing separately for the last more than 15 years and they have no issue from this wedlock.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not grant restitution of conjugal rights if the parties have no issue from their marriage.
legal_principles.held: It is also not in dispute the parties are residing separately for the last more than 15 years and they have no issue from this wedlock.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court are set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petitions under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on Family Courts Act procedures
assisting with cross-objections in divorce cases
